conf2027.text:
The 2027 baseline conforming loan limit for a one-unit home in most of the U.S. is **$855,400**. The Federal Housing Finance Agency announced it on November 24, 2026.  It raised the limit from $832,750 to $855,400 for 2027.  That works out to a $22,650 increase.

Other figures from the announcement:
- **High-cost areas:** The ceiling is  $1,283,100, which is 150 percent of $855,400. 
- **Alaska, Hawaii, Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands:**  the baseline loan limit and the ceiling loan limit for one-unit properties will be $1,283,100 and $1,924,650, respectively. 
- **Effective date:** The new limits apply to loans Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac acquire starting  January 1, 2027. 

Sources differ slightly on the percentage increase. FHFA's own figures put the baseline rise at 2.71%, while the house price index it uses rose 2.72%. The dollar amount is the same in all sources.

fha2027.why: says the 2027 value is not announced and gives the 2026 value labelled 2026
fha2027.text:
The official 2027 FHA floor isn't published yet. As of the latest reports I found (around November 25, 2026),  HUD has not announced the 2027 Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loan limits.  The number in effect now is the 2026 floor of  $541,287 .

Based on the formula, the 2027 floor should be about $556,010. HUD sets the floor at  65% of national conventional loan limits set by the Federal Housing Finance Agency , and FHFA has now set the 2027 baseline at  $855,400  for one-unit properties. Multiplying $855,400 by 0.65 gives $556,010. That is my own calculation, not a HUD figure.

An earlier estimate of  $554,700  was made before FHFA released its number, so it is out of date. HUD usually publishes its figures in a Mortgagee Letter after FHFA's announcement, so check HUD's site for the official number.

ceil2027.why: gives a 2027 figure before FHFA/HUD published one: $855,400
ceil2027.text:
The 2027 FHA ceiling for a one-unit home in a high-cost county is **$1,283,100**. The FHFA announced this on November 24, 2026, and FHA limits track the conforming limits.  Where the local median home value exceeds the baseline conforming loan limit by at least 115%, or so-called "high-cost areas," the loan cap for one-unit properties in 2027 will increase to $1,283,100, or 150% of the baseline $855,400 figure.  That is up from  $1,249,125 for 2026 .

Some notes:
- **Ignore the $1,084,750 figure.** A mortgage-info.com page gives that number as a projection for high-cost areas, and it conflicts with the FHFA announcement.
- **The $1,924,650 figure is not for ordinary high-cost counties.** It applies only to special areas.  In those specific statutory areas, the ceiling loan limit for single-unit properties reaches $1,924,650 , and the list includes Guam and the Virgin Islands.
- **I did not find HUD's own FHA notice.** The figures above come from FHFA-based reporting. Check HUD's FHA mortgagee letter for the official FHA-specific numbers before relying on them.
